extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy / Plato (general readers and scholars)
extracted.subtask_description: Normative prescriptions for organizing the guardian class in an ideal city: who may be guardians, how men and women are educated and share duties, rules for marriage and breeding, property, and family arrangements to maximize unity and the common good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal education for men and women
rubrics_metrics.description: If women are to have the same duties as men, they must have the same nurture and education; the education which was assigned to the men was music and gymnastic, and then women must be taught music and gymnastic and also the art of war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: men and women differ in strength but not in the kinds of pursuits they can be trained for; therefore, women who are to be guardians should receive the same training (music, gymnastics, military arts) so they can perform the same functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection by natural gifts, not by sex
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no special faculty of administration in a state which a woman has because she is a woman, or which a man has by virtue of his sex; the gifts of nature are alike diffused in both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians should be chosen because they possess the qualities of guardianship (temper, spirit, capacity), regardless of sex; women with those qualities should be selected as companions and colleagues of similar men.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women to share guardians' pursuits with adjusted labour
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the wives of our guardians strip, for their virtue will be their robe, and let them share in the toils of war and the defence of their country; only in the distribution of labours the lighter are to be assigned to the women, who are the weaker natures, but in other respects their duties are to be the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledges physical differences but maintains common civic duties; women participate in military and civic life with proportionate assignments where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common houses and common meals for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: They must live in common houses and meet at common meals. None of them will have anything specially his or her own; they will be together, and will be brought up together, and will associate at gymnastic exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communal living is intended to produce unity of feeling and to prevent private interests from dividing the guardians.

rubrics_metrics.name: No private property for guardians; pay limited to sustenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The guardians were not to have houses or lands or any other property; their pay was to be their food, which they were to receive from the other citizens, and they were to have no private expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community of property aims to remove quarrels over 'mine' and 'not mine' and to keep guardians focused on the common good rather than private gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community of wives and children; parents not to know their own children
rubrics_metrics.description: The wives of our guardians are to be common, and their children are to be common, and no parent is to know his own child, nor any child his parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed to strengthen unity: family ties become civic ties; the scheme includes procedures to prevent parental recognition and private family loyalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled breeding: unite best with best, limit inferior unions
rubrics_metrics.description: The best of either sex should be united with the best as often, and the inferior with the inferior, as seldom as possible; they should rear the offspring of the one sort of union, but not of the other, if the flock is to be maintained in first-rate condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulers must manage pairings to preserve the quality of the guardian class — including selective rearing and withholding offspring of inferior unions from the citizen body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulers may lawfully use falsehood and deceit for the good of the state
rubrics_metrics.description: Our rulers will find a considerable dose of falsehood and deceit necessary for the good of their subjects: we were saying that the use of all these things regarded as medicines might be of advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Noble lies’ or controlled untruths are justified as therapeutic measures for maintaining social order and preventing unrest when implementing sensitive policies (e.g., about parentage, breeding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public festivals and ritualised pairing organized by rulers
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint certain festivals at which we will bring together the brides and bridegrooms, and sacrifices will be offered and suitable hymeneal songs composed by our poets: the number of weddings is a matter which must be left to the discretion of the rulers, whose aim will be to preserve the average of population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pairings and births are to be ritualized and socially regulated; population controls consider effects of war, disease, etc., and should be administered by officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lots to mask rulers' choices for pairing among less worthy
rubrics_metrics.description: We shall have to invent some ingenious kind of lots which the less worthy may draw on each occasion of our bringing them together, and then they will accuse their own ill-luck and not the rulers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mechanism to preserve rulers' control while avoiding blame: apparent randomness conceals deliberate selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal or concealment of offspring judged unfit
rubrics_metrics.description: The offspring of the inferior, or of the better when they chance to be deformed, will be put away in some mysterious, unknown place, as they should be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To maintain the quality of the guardian stock, deformed or inferior children are to be disposed of secretly and removed from the citizen body (presented here as necessary for the state's health).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of nurses and limitation of maternal contact
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper officers will take the offspring of the good parents to the pen or fold, and there they will deposit them with certain nurses who dwell in a separate quarter; ... Care will also be taken that the process of suckling shall not be protracted too long; and the mothers will have no getting up at night or other trouble, but will hand over all this sort of thing to the nurses and attendants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids strong parental bonds that could create private loyalties; childrearing is professionalized and separated from the biological parents for civic unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined procreative age ranges and sanction for out-of-age unions
rubrics_metrics.description: A woman at twenty years of age may begin to bear children to the State, and continue to bear them until forty; a man may begin at five-and-twenty ... and continue to beget children until he be fifty-five. Any one above or below the prescribed ages who takes part in the public hymeneals shall be said to have done an unholy and unrighteous thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Age windows for sanctioned procreation are prescribed to ensure physical and civic fitness; unions outside these ranges are condemned and their offspring treated as illegitimate or to be prevented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social re-labelling of kinship by ritual timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Dating from the day of the hymeneal, the bridegroom who was then married will call all the male children who are born in the seventh and tenth month afterwards his sons, and the female children his daughters... All who were begotten at the time when their fathers and mothers came together will be called their brothers and sisters, and these ... will be forbidden to inter-marry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kinship is defined by institutional ritual and timing rather than biological parentage; this constructs civic family relationships and regulates marriage among guardians (with limited oracle exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of close-kin marriages (with civic definitions/exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A man may not marry his daughter or his daughter’s daughter, or his mother or his mother’s mother; and women ... are prohibited from marrying their sons or fathers, or son’s son or father’s father, and so on ... This, however, is not to be understood as an absolute prohibition of the marriage of brothers and sisters; if the lot favours them, and they receive the sanction of the Pythian oracle, the law will allow them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incest prohibitions are enforced according to the civic kinship scheme, but extraordinary oracle-sanctioned exceptions may be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must obey laws and model them
rubrics_metrics.description: The guardians must themselves obey the laws, and they must also imitate the spirit of them in any details which are entrusted to their care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral authority of rulers requires they be exemplars of the laws they enforce; willingness to obey and power to command must coexist among rulers and auxiliaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common property and family as means to civic unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the community of property and the community of families ... tend to make them more truly guardians; they will not tear the city in pieces by differing about 'mine' and 'not mine'... all will be affected as far as may be by the same pleasures and pains because they are all of one opinion about what is near and dear to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: shared possessions and familial relations produce shared pleasures/pains, minimizing factionalism and maximizing unity of feeling in the polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social mechanisms (shame and fear) and elder authority to prevent internal violence
rubrics_metrics.description: To the elder shall be assigned the duty of ruling and chastising the younger. Nor can there be a doubt that the younger will not strike or do any other violence to an elder, unless the magistrates command him; for there are two guardians, shame and fear, mighty to prevent him: shame ... and fear, that the injured one will be succoured by the others who are his brothers, sons, fathers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal order is maintained by hierarchical duties, communal solidarity, and social sanctions rather than private retaliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim of legislation: unity of feeling and the greatest good
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief aim of the legislator in making laws and in the organization of a State is to prevent discord where unity ought to reign; unity comes from community of pleasures and pains where all the citizens are glad or grieved on the same occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative principle underlying the proposals: policies (education, communal property/families, rituals) are justified insofar as they produce civic unity and the common good, analogous to harmony in a single body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians' lifestyle prioritized over private notions of happiness
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of our guardians shall try to be happy in such a manner that he will cease to be a guardian ... he will have to learn ... 'half is more than the whole.' Stay where you are, when you have the offer of such a life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guardians should accept the specially regulated, communal life as the highest form of happiness appropriate to their role; private ambition or appropriation of the state undermines their duty and is condemned.
